mappings.note: Sex determination by XX/XY. C3.3 for the chromosomal mechanism; C4.4 because the item is a pattern of inheritance of a trait. No learning outcome exists under either, which is why both are cited at competency level.

Menstrual hygiene practices. This is the reproductive-health limb of the fused LO-10 row, not cycle physiology, which is why this item gets a code while the other menstrual items in this chapter fall back to C3.2.

POOR FIT. Emotional versus sexual maturity. C5.2 (science in human life from the perspective of Social Sciences and Ethics) is the nearest legal container. LO-10 rejected: its subject is contraceptive devices, and nothing about contraception is in this item.
Which STI is not curable. Reaches LO-10 only through the reproductive-health clause fused into that row; the frame records no STI outcome of its own.
Four contraceptive methods judged for correctness. The core, unstrained use of LO-10: barrier, hormonal, intra-uterine and surgical devices are exactly what the outcome names.
Finds the false statement about the Copper-T, the error being that it is a barrier method. Same outcome as the other IUD items; split from them only by being the negative-stem form.

Prenatal sex determination law and sex-ratio imbalance. C5.2 for the law-and-ethics framing; C4.4 because the consequence examined is at population level. LO-10 rejected: no contraceptive device is involved, and stretching its population-control clause here would make it mean anything demographic.
The CDRI non-hormonal oral contraceptive. LO-10 for the device, C6.1 for the Indian contribution. LO-12 rejected (it names Maheshwari and plant tissue culture) and LO-11 rejected (human anatomy).
Defines vegetative propagation. The C3.2 process twin; nothing genetic is asked, so not LO-9, unlike the immediately following item on clones.

The significance of producing clones. The heredity twin, and the direct contrast with the preceding definition item that takes LO-7. These two adjacent items are the cleanest demonstration of the LO-7/LO-9 split rule.
Names two methods of vegetative propagation. Method recall, C3.2 twin.
Names a plant that propagates through leaves. Method and organ recall; shares LO-7 with the MCQ version of the same Bryophyllum fact earlier in the chapter.
The role of spores in fungal reproduction. Asexual mode, so LO-7; this is the same outcome as the other four spore items, which honestly share it.
Defines meiosis. No meiosis outcome exists; the mechanism-of-heredity competency is the ceiling. Not C-3.3-LO-5, which is about variation and is not what a definition asks for.
Why meiosis is essential: restoring diploid number on fusion. Constancy, not variation, so the competency rather than C-3.3-LO-5.

Sepals versus petals. LO-8 does not reach either, since neither is a male or female reproductive organ; C-5.1-LO-1 covers the structure of the flower as a reproductive unit, and is the same choice made for the outermost-whorl MCQ.
The female whorl and its three parts. This IS a female reproductive organ, so LO-8, in contrast with the sepal-and-petal item immediately before it, which is not.
The immediate result of fertilisation is a zygote. The fertilisation limb of LO-4; stops before the seed, so not C-3.2-LO-3.
Failure of pollen transfer (LO-4) with the consequence stated as no seeds and no fruits (LO-3). Both outcomes are cited because the item spans exactly the boundary between them.
Self versus cross pollination in one line. Same outcome as the MCQ version; the family shares it because they differ only in format.
Where external fertilisation happens. The fertilisation limb of LO-4; the frame has no separate outcome for reproductive strategy in animals.
The advantage of internal fertilisation. The mode of fertilisation is the whole answer, so LO-4.
Why fish and frogs lay many eggs. Third member of the external-fertilisation egg-number family, which genuinely shares this outcome; only the format differs.
Function of the testes. Male reproductive organ description, so LO-8, in contrast with the scrotum item that follows, which asks about position rather than function but lands on the same outcome.
Where the testes sit and why. Male reproductive organ anatomy under LO-8; the thermal reasoning has no outcome of its own, but the organ is what the student must name.
